newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds quiet, British Land bond sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds quiet, British Land bond sharply higher.

text.p: The primary market was fairly quiet on Thursday morning with just a handful of small, retail-targeted deals to keep syndicate desks ticking over.

British Land's 300 million stg convertible bond, launched Tuesday, has rallied to 104.50 bid on broker screens, giving a paper profit of 7.0 percentage points, or just over 20 million stg for those involved in the deal.
"The whole tone of the market has changed. The price tells you all you need to know," a banker at SBC Warburg, the 10-year deal's sole manager, said.
On Wednesday, in an almost unprecedented move in the Eurobond market, SBC Warburg delivered a downbeat assessment of its own issue.
It said in a statement that "demand for the convertible did not develop as hoped in deteriorating market conditions".
British Land's share price shed 23 pence stg, or 3.94 percent on Tuesday, outstripping the FTSE-100 index's 0.82 percent fall.
British Land has since bounced back to rise above 600p this morning and set a fresh record high at 610p in the process.
The SBC Warburg banker said the price had never fallen below the par issue price despite the initial poor demand.
The 680p conversion price on the convertible bond is just 12.5 percent above the mid-market price, against 21.2 percent when final terms were set on Tuesday.
British property stocks have been buoyant since Land Securities announced profits at the top end of expectations on Wednesday.
Land Securites issued a 210 million stg convertible in January on which SBC Warburg was one of the joint lead managers.
Elsewhere, Nafinsa set a $150 million three-year Eurobond via BZW which will price the deal later today at an indicated 135-140 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
